- Link every GitHub issue and pull request you mention, in chat and docs. Only GitHub's own UI turns a bare number into a link.

Two guardrails hold Melian's documents to the writing rules in `AGENTS.md`. Each is `P3`, which is advisory. Problem: Melian's own reviews raised both findings five or more times, and a lens spends model calls on what a pattern can see. `bare-issue-reference` reads a `#` and digits in every Markdown file but `.github/` and the goldens. The `#` must follow the start of a line, a space, or `(`, and no `]`, word character, or `-` may follow the digits. Example: a hash and digits after a space fire, and a number that a `]` follows, as in link text, does not. Without lookaround the rule cannot tell link text from prose. A number inside the text of a longer link fires. A number after a quote mark or a backtick, such as `melian review "#41"`, does not. `overlong-sentence` reads 45 or more words in a row on one line, in `docs/`, the comparison records, and `README.md`. A full stop, question mark, exclamation mark, or `|` ends the run. Example: a sentence of 60 words fires, and one of 24 does not. A word is a run of word characters, apostrophes, backticks, and hyphens. The pattern counts words instead of skipping up to 40 characters between them, because each repeat costs steps against the engine's 2,000-step cap. A line is the unit, so a list item that runs on with no mark fires. A table bar ends the run, so each cell is measured alone. A semicolon or colon does not end it, because clauses joined by either read as one sentence. An earlier version let a 100-word sentence of semicolons pass, and the conventions lens flagged it. A full stop inside a version number or a path ends it as well. Both rules sit in the root `melian.yaml` and carry a `severity`, which is why a rule can set one. `packages/core/test/doc-guardrails.test.ts` pins them, and the `guardrails-bare-issue-reference` and `guardrails-overlong-sentence` goldens run each through a review.

evidence.snippet: verdicts.push({ verdict: findings, own: round.revision === gate });

The first draft settled two records in one slot by the lowest ID. [Issue #378](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/378) showed a writer could grind an ID to win a slot, and Melian's own design lens showed two honest hosts losing a blocking sighting that way, since two runs of one lens can differ. So:

- **A round names what it rests on.** Its closing record lists the kind, key and ID of every record it read, its walkthrough or that it has none, the earlier rounds of its revision it replaces, and the rounds of the revision before. A record a round names counts for that round. One that does not match the named kind, key and ID together counts as not found, and a round with a record not found reads as not reviewed.
- **An import keeps every record.** A host that finds several trusted records under the key its own run would use imports all of them, and their sightings merge as two lenses' sightings do. Nothing is dropped. The merge keeps [its order](2026-10-16-merge-by-shared-cause.md), the most severe as reported and then the lens. Two runs of one lens tie on both, and the record's ID breaks that tie. Every claim is kept and the highest severity among them counts, so the ID decides which prose speaks, and never whether a claim or a severity counts.
- **Standing is computed from the rounds.** A round of a revision stands when no round that counts names it as replaced. Nothing else says which round is current, so there is no pointer for a writer to roll back. Where a key is pinned, only a round that key signed counts, so only the trusted host's round can replace the trusted host's.
- **The gate takes the worst standing round.** Two rounds that stand together, because two hosts reviewed at once, gate by the worse, and not reviewed is worse than blocking.

## The residual accepted

A failure the head itself causes only sometimes, such as a test that hangs on a race, reads as `failed` in one round and clean in another, and the gate passes on the clean one. Worst-of would block it. The maintainer accepted this, as `--rerun` accepts it on a host today.

What bounds it:

- A check's `failed` status says the check did not finish, not that it found something. Anything a check finds is a finding, and findings are pooled at their strictest, so a clean run hides only that another run did not finish.
- Only a round of exactly M..H covers. A round of an older base contributes findings, never coverage.
- Only a writer can add a round to `melian/state`, and the gate counts no record of a fork's head.
- A round whose verifier failed covers nothing, and a lens below the base tip's floor covers nothing. So the round that stands in for a failed check is one the host itself would read as reviewed, at the level the base tip asks for now.

It stays in the merged verdict at advisory (record-gate.ts:222-225), is never silenced, and appears in the gate's output. Only a trusted writer can add round B to the store, and B must itself be sound, with its verifier run and every tier check covered at the floor (record-gate.ts:273-310). The head decision records this as an accepted residual (lines 32-41). So it is a narrowed weakening of a fail-closed rule, not an unconditional merge of an unjudged P1.

Status is "not-reviewed" only if `notRun` is non-empty, and `notRun` is built from `covered`, which any sound round of M..H can fill (lines 156, 170-176). Round A's refusal for a failed verifier (lines 307-309) therefore takes away only A's coverage. Its P1 still counts, capped at advisory, and `passes()` ignores advisory findings (lines 197-202).
